status: Reviewed source-fit authoring coverage of two selected clauses; not learner attainment or a full regional demographic study.

resources.date: Membership table July2022; annual housing report2021–22
facts: Published total-column Nation-member counts: Garden Village478, Yellek199 and Duchesnay183. These selected on-reserve member groups have different reported numbers; they are not all residents of those places.
The same report separately gives homes: Garden Village223, Yellek Village159 and Duchesnay Village123. Homes are not people.
limits: Nation membership and census resident population are different defined populations. Do not combine them, infer household size or compare their percentages as if equivalent.
The report also lists off-reserve members; selected community counts do not represent all Nation members or all residents.

An inconsistency exists in the gender-column arithmetic of the source totals. Use the selected published community total column, not reconstructed grand totals or repaired data. Counts do not establish population density.

resources.publisher: Municipality of West Nipissing, commissioned market study
facts: The actual labelled community-location map places Garden Village on the western part of the mapped lake-shore area and Yellek and Duchesnay on the eastern part. It supports locating the selected community-count groups.
limits: Use this older map only for the named community locations. Do not substitute its historical area/community totals for current Nation accounts or treat its outline as traditional territory or legal adjudication.
The adjacent West Nipissing municipal census table concerns a different jurisdiction and population. It must not be attached to the Nation community symbols.

facts: The actual Garden Village nature-trail map identifies a walking route through the wooded part of the selected local area near roads and developed places.

The Nation describes roads connecting its communities, business locations and a commercial/light-industrial business park. These accounts identify transport, recreation and work uses beyond appearance.
limits: The small trail map is a selected-place recreation reference, not an exhaustive land-use map or readable parcel inventory.

Different report dates remain visible. A future project mentioned in an older report is not certified complete by that report. Member/affiliate access rules for a selected recreation site are not replaced by a universal public-access claim.

resources.publisher: City of Niagara Falls; published Statistics Canada census layer
facts: The actual layer is explicitly population COUNT by census dissemination area2021. Its key has five count classes:98–468,469–716,717–1209,1210–1931,1932–5313.

The rendered map shows differently sized areas with different count classes. A large south-central polygon is in the highest class, while many smaller central/eastern polygons are in lower classes. Each colour summarises a whole dissemination area.
limits: The areas are unequal in size. A darker or larger polygon does not by itself mean higher density, an evenly spread population or more crowded homes. No synthetic density legend is supplied.
The older2016density layer has a suspect published label/unit relationship and is excluded rather than silently repaired.
Provide the actual class key, year, north reference, municipal location labels and defined population with the rendered map; the raw unlabelled export alone is not the finished teaching packet.

facts: The actual service identifies existing park and trail lands and public trail lines. It includes City and other owners, such as Niagara Parks Commission, and explicitly excludes proposed park/trail lands.
The rendered map shows selected recreation patches and linked corridors, including river-side routes; these can be compared with the Garden Village selected nature-trail map.
limits: Unshaded land is not automatically residential or unused. This is not an exhaustive land-use inventory.
Do not infer every park is City-owned or unrestricted at every time. No area fraction or relative trail length is inferred from differently scaled images.

facts: The previously reviewed actual Ontario map locates North Bay/Nipissing and Niagara Falls for broad regional orientation. Use a globe to locate Canada and Ontario before placing the two selected regional cases.
limits: The Canada Lands index is not a traditional-territory map. Keep its own main map/key/scale together; do not mix the inset scale.

population-and-use-patterns.preparation: Provide the actual source maps with readable labels and original keys; adult-added own teaching annotations must be clearly distinguished. Place the dated selected Nation-member community table beside its location map, and the2021Niagara census count key beside the actual DA map. Retain source dates, different populations and map extents. Supply actual-use accounts and the two selected trail/park maps.
actions: Locate Canada/Ontario on a globe, then locate the Nipissing/North Bay and Niagara areas on the reviewed Ontario map. Identify the selected community labels and the north/key conventions on each detailed map.

Describe at least one supported within-region distribution pattern for EACH region. For the selected Nation-member groups, locate Garden Village versus Yellek/Duchesnay and compare their published counts. State that these are member counts by selected community, not all residents. For Niagara, locate a higher-count DA and lower-count DAs using the actual key; state that each number/class is a resident count for a differently sized area, not a density or uniform dot distribution.

Use the Nation actual-use accounts and selected trail map, and Niagara actual park/trail inventory plus previously reviewed Dufferin recreation account, to identify some land-use patterns in both regions. Relate named recreation, transport, housing and work uses only where supported by the source; do not label every unshaded place.

Construct a small labelled thematic comparison map or two-panel map with a key for the selected count groups and supported uses. Keep population symbols separate from land-use categories. Explain one relative location and why blank/unclassified land is not necessarily unused.
population-and-use-patterns.positive: Describes supported population-count distributions and some actual land-use patterns in both regions, including the Nation case, using maps plus broad globe orientation and correct population/date/area units.
nearMiss: Treats Nation membership as the complete resident census or houses as people.
Calls the highest-count Niagara DA the most densely populated from colour alone.
Infers a residential use from every unshaded polygon.
population-and-use-patterns.transfer: Interpret a newly selected labelled area from the same sources or a comparable verified local packet, explaining the population definition and one key-supported pattern rather than memorising colours.

actions: Compare selected documented recreation and transport uses in the two regions: the Garden Village wooded walking route and connecting-road account versus the Niagara actual mapped park/trail corridors and selected shoreline recreation work. State one similarity and one difference using actual map/account evidence.

Bring in the reported Nation housing locations only as a selected housing example, not a count comparison against an unrelated Niagara total. Explain how housing, roads and recreation serve needs, and why wooded/open land can have a purpose.

If comparing size or number, choose a like-for-like explicitly defined source unit with appropriate matching map scales; otherwise compare supported location/purpose rather than inventing exhaustive amounts. The source requires some aspects, not every illustrative use or a regional land-use census.
compare-selected-uses.positive: Uses particular source evidence to compare some actual land-use aspects in two places, including a First Nation community, without confusing dates, membership, ownership or incomplete inventories.
nearMiss: Compares apparent feature size across mismatched map scales.
Calls the two cases identical merely because each has a park.
compare-selected-uses.transfer: Explain what extra evidence would be needed before claiming a new unlabelled place is housing or before comparing total recreation areas.

wholeClaimAndSourceLimits: Map reading and construction remain the unchanged whole map claim; the packet includes labels, a key and relative-location explanation. Its retained hard prerequisites remain separately assessed.

Land-purpose reasoning remains the unchanged whole land-use claim, including water/unbuilt/mixed-use distinctions in its existing canonical assessment. The selected local tasks are components, not automatic certification of every source example or whole-topic mastery.

Population distribution here is described using explicitly defined count groups and their locations. This is not a density study, inference of exact individuals, or a demographic equivalence between the two source populations.

No new collection/statistics claim is proposed just because the packet contains numbers; dataset acquisition, spreadsheets and a separate full graphing assessment are not imported into these two source clauses.

This design accounts for authoring requirements, not observed learner success or a current regional census. B1/B3 integrated dispositions remain separately pending completion of their remaining selected clauses.
